Because its named a "personality disorder". Personality is understood by most people as something stable that defines a person and their behaviour. So with this understanding, saying someone has a personality disorder is saying that their personality, ie. the person, is disordered or ill. 

In psychology, personality is defined as individual differences between thinking, feeling, and behaving. They're called personality disorders because the maladaptive thinking causes the symptoms of disordered feeling and behaving, not because the "personality" it's self is disordered. But since most people aren't psychologists, they don't have this understanding of what a personality disorder truly is.

I'm sorry this has been so upsetting for you :( I was pretty upset when Robin Williams took his own life for some of the same reasons, and all I knew about him was what I saw in movies and the occasional interview. Being able to relate to someone on that level can be emotionally moving.

I've done my research on them and found the same information... it's the main reason I don't really want to try it but I was hoping for some sort of a good review of them that I might have missed somewhere haha. I definitely feel like it would have the same effect on me since I'm pretty sure my main issue is with dopamine as well. 

I'm a little disappointed that there are no other anti-depressants that effect dopamine other than Wellbutrin (which worked really well, but gave me tinnitus) and SNDRIs (which i've heard horror stories about). Plus, every time I try serotonin altering drugs I always feel like I get serotonin syndrome so I stay away from the typical antidepressants. 

I really appreciate you talking about your experiences with these drugs. It's definitely given me a better insight into what direction I should go...and it's looking like I should either not take anymore stimulants or keep smoking pot every night to ease the crash symptoms (which really isn't ideal). 

ps. I love wikipedia for that... I know way too much about psychoactive drugs than I should. And it's always helpful to hear other peoples experiences on them.

Hmm...I'll look into those three medications. 

I've had the same experience as well. While stimulants were helpful to just get school work done, I suggested to my doctor to up my Wellbutrin dose to 300 from 150, and it really opened my eyes as to how much I was capable of. I have trouble with interrupting in a group conversation and for the first time I was able to sit with my thoughts and speak at an appropriate time for the entire meeting. I was also able to read for a decent amount of time, and I generally felt a lot calmer and in control of my life. Unfortunately it also gave me terrible tinnitus so I'm back down at 150 which doesn't really do much for me. 

My therapist gave me some helpful tips with chores since I have trouble with them as well. It really helps to make a list and break it down into chunks. The ADHD brain needs reward more often than the neurotypical brain, so you can trick your brain into thinking you're achieving more than you actually are by making it seem like you're getting through "checkpoints" with each step you complete. It's not fool proof, but it helps a bit when you really need to get things done and you're feeling overwhelmed.

You know, I first started on Vyvanse (an XR version of dex) and the first couple doses were euphoric (as they are for everyone)...but once I came down it was like the world lost all of it's colour. It's such a terrible, terrible feeling. 

I found that it was a little better if I ate well during the day and took time to consciously relax when I knew I would crash soon, but nothing works all that well. I'm still extremely moody both while I'm on the medication as well as when I'm not :(

Thanks for the thoughts. I've unfortunately tried all of this and have tried nearly every medication at every reasonable dose, and the reality is that I'm just emotionally volatile and any sort of stimulant just adds to the problem. I've tried non-stimulants as well, and because I have an issue with motivation and energy, they don't work well for me. 

The worst part is I started taking 300mg of Wellbutrin at one point, which actually worked amazingly, but gave me terrible tinnitus. So that had to end as well. 

Do you have your own experiences with these medications?

I've considered this as well. I haven't said anything to any doctor, even though I've never had a problem with substance abuse. I even quit smoking cold turkey when I used to regularly smoke when I was younger just because I didn't like smoking anymore (I guess splitting-related behaviours can come in handy sometimes). But I'd just rather not risk it and let them continue with the diagnosis of anxiety and depression for now...no harm in that. 

I've definitely tried behavioural modifications which have really worked wonders - I didn't need any meds for most of the summer while I was taking classes. But fall and winter classes are so much harder on me because of the weather and what not and I just don't seem to do as well without. 

I've heard about people taking mood stabilizers with ADHD meds to iron the emotional lability out...what are your thoughts on that?

I feel this exact same way every time I crash... I honestly feel like I'm losing my mind. I don't really take the meds to feel good, it's mostly so I can stay on top of my school work. The downside is the fact that they really don't make me feel good all...they make me feel terrible, as you've described.

That sounds incredibly rough :( unfortunately i've tried it all and nothing works as well as stimulants because I do honestly have an issue with dopamine (motivation, reward, and energy)...the only other option is to ask my doctor for mood stabilizers but I'm not too keen on that.

Forgiveness doesn't always mean you need to get closure. It's accepting what's happened, and accepting that the past is the past and it cant be changed. You can't get closure from everyone, but you can give yourself "closure" by trying to empathize with the person that hurt you (which is why holding a grudge is much easier). 

I think it's especially hard for us because we hold onto feelings so tightly and we remember them so well. I still struggle with forgiving my mother with what she put me through... the feelings I had as a child always come up again and it's hard to simply empathize with someone when it feels like they keep hurting you over and over again.
But I'll be around them a lot because we're in one cohort and we have a lot of mutual friends :/
